title: Sorrify-at-failure in the failed Tapir to SSER refinement (tapir_refines_sser)
intent: Records the Section 6.3 falsification attempt for Tapir: the author decomposes tapir_refines_sser into an event induction plus four per-event abs_committed_reads bookkeeping lemmas that all close, while the harder obligations (fp_property, the kvs_of_s update, and the Cl_ReadyC, Commit and Abort cases) are left as sorry with comments naming the invariant still needed. The entry shows which children of a plausible decomposition were sufficient, and which were not, and why.

parent.name: tapir_refines_sser
parent.statement: tapir refines ET_SSER.ET_ES up to the simulation relation sim and mediator med

children.name: read_resp_abs_committed_reads_inv
children.statement: abs_committed_reads is unchanged when a read-response moves the server entry for Tn t from idle to read X

children.name: prep_abs_committed_reads_inv
children.statement: abs_committed_reads is unchanged when a prepare moves the server entry for Tn t from read X to occ_check (client still prepared)

children.name: commit_abs_committed_reads_inv
children.statement: abs_committed_reads is unchanged when a commit moves the server entry for Tn t from prepared to committed, for a key in the client's read map

children.name: abort_abs_committed_reads_inv
children.statement: abs_committed_reads is unchanged when an abort moves the server entry for Tn t to aborted

applicability.goal_shape: A refinement P refines Q up to a simulation relation sim and a mediator med, proved by a simulation relation (intro simulate_ES_fun_h) followed by induction over the event constructors; each event case must exhibit the abstract transition, and the invariant the simulation relation depends on (here abs_committed_reads) must be preserved by every event.
applicability.use_when: A mostly-working decomposition has a few cases or obligations that will not close, and you want to keep the proved lemmas while recording exactly which sub-goals fail and what extra invariant each needs (the author's comments name it).
applicability.avoid_when: The shared invariant is too weak in the first place: sorrifying the failures hides that the decomposition itself must be strengthened (a stronger invariant stated as its own lemma) rather than patched per case.

claims.claim: tapir_refines_sser is declared in VerIso/Tapir_Falsification.thy, lines 434-435.
The glue of tapir_refines_sser spans 130 lines (434-563) and its four direct children span 8, 9, 11 and 9 lines (18-25, 27-35, 37-47, 49-57), so the longest lemma chain below the theorem is 1.
claims.evidence: Line arithmetic on the parent and child sites (declaration through closing by/qed) in the copied file VerIso/Tapir_Falsification.thy at commit 6407b72; 434-563 is 130 lines, and 18-25, 27-35, 37-47, 49-57 are 8, 9, 11, 9 lines.

metrics.how_counted: sorry = occurrences of the keyword 'sorry' in VerIso/Tapir_Falsification.thy (grep -c sorry); the four child lemmas each close by 'by (auto simp add: abs_committed_reads_def)'

consequences: Replacing a failing block with sorry keeps the statement and lets the file compile, but leaves a hole: the theorem is unproved and the file no longer establishes the refinement. Each hole's obligation must be re-derived from a stronger invariant; the comments name them: 'no transactions after t_wr have written a new version to server k' and 'no prepared (but client-committed) newer versions are on server k' (fp_property), 'new (uncommitted) write is not read by any transactions' (Cl_ReadyC), 'newly committed version's readerset is empty' (Commit), and 'aborted txn not in commit_order' (Abort). The four bookkeeping lemmas all share the shape 'a state update leaves abs_committed_reads unchanged' and close by unfolding abs_committed_reads_def alone, which is why they were easy; the failing cases need facts about other transactions, which the invariant abs_committed_reads does not capture.
